summary: Real but unproven problem with no demand evidence, and the buyer (agency owners) needs outbound sales David has no network for and doesn't want. It repeats the cure-vs-prevention weakness that sank feedwarden and listvault and competes with Little Warden's low price.

demand.evidence: Only vendor or secondhand numbers (Leadferno 4.8% broken forms, original not located; PageCrawl anecdote; unnamed 48% Consent Mode claim). No one has asked for or paid for this.

statusQuo.evidence: Agencies already pay for audits and monitoring (Inflow $1,999, freelancer EUR 150-250/mo, Little Warden GBP 59.99/mo, Trackingplan $249/mo), but Little Warden undercuts the planned $149/mo.

specificity.evidence: Target is 'agency owner or account lead', a category. No named person; David has no agency network and wants no sales calls.

wedge.evidence: $500 one-time audit is the right wedge, but passive checks only show 'suspect' not 'broken'; the convincing test submission is deferred to M5.

futureFit.evidence: Consent Mode and server-side tagging add complexity, but Google diagnostics, Little Warden and AI QA tools absorb the checks; no moat.

premises: Agencies lose leads and ad spend to silent form and tag breakage: plausible, frequency unmeasured
A 'happening now' audit overcomes cure-vs-prevention: unsupported
Passive checks are convincing enough to sell: contradicted by the research's own risks
Agencies pay above Little Warden's price for evidence reports: unsupported
David can reach agency buyers without sales calls: contradicted by the research
alternatives: Minimal: free public 'check your site' tool, one URL in and a report out, to test whether anyone cares
Ideal: full monitoring SaaS with scheduled diffs, agency index and opt-in test submissions (large, runs into Little Warden pricing)
Lateral: fold tag and form checks into an existing repo of David's (RepoHQ site health or the AEM Page Tracker) instead of a new product
wedge: One URL in, one shareable HTML evidence report out, no signup, with a human-checked $500 audit offered in the footer.

feasibility.notes: Node + Playwright, GitHub Actions, Vercel Hobby, Resend free. Proving test: fixture with GA4 snippet but blocked collect request is flagged, and a form fixture asserts zero POSTs. This proves the tool works, not that anyone wants it.

risks: No demand evidence; all numbers are vendor or secondhand
Buyer needs outbound sales; David has no network and avoids calls
Passive checks give false positives and cannot prove a broken form
Unsolicited audits read as cold outreach
Same cure-vs-prevention failure as feedwarden and listvault
killCriteria: Drop if under 10% of 100 audited agency-client sites show an actionable finding; false positives exceed 20% on 50 checked findings; fewer than 3 of 30 agencies reply to a sample report; no one pays the $500 audit within 30 days; or buyers only accept Little Warden pricing.
